History:
- Chief complaint: New severe headache for about 3 days.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began ~3 days ago at work; gradually worsened; pain present most of the time with fluctuations; currently described as 8/10 and persistent.
- Location/quality: Headache all over, mainly around the right eye; dull pain with occasional sharper moments.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia (light worsens symptoms), light sensitivity, nausea (no vomiting), neck stiffness, difficulty focusing; no vision loss or weakness; no speech difficulties; no fever or rash.
- Triggers/context: Onset during work; possible stress with a new project and heavy computer use; attempted ibuprofen without meaningful relief.
- History of headaches/migraine: Patient has had headaches before; has not had migraines herself; mother and sister have migraines.
- Medications/allergies: No regular medications; used ibuprofen for 2 days (three tablets per day); no known drug allergies.
- Social history: Social smoker and social drinker; lives with three housemates; works in IT; wears glasses; notes screen brightness and eye strain.
- Eye history: Wears glasses since childhood; no recent eye exam reported.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: none documented
- Allergies: none documented
- Medications: none regularly; short-term ibuprofen used
- Prior hospitalizations: none documented

Physical Examination (reported/patient-observed findings):
- Neck stiffness: present
- Photophobia/light sensitivity: present
- Visual symptoms: light sensitivity; no vision loss; no blurred vision; difficulty focusing
- Neurologic: no weakness; no speech difficulties noted
- Constitutional: no fever; no rash; no vomiting
- Additional: patient displays headache symptoms consistent with self-reported history; no other exam findings documented
- Vitals: not documented

Impression:
- Headache with features suggestive of migraine-type headache given photophobia, unilateral/right-eye predominance, nausea, neck stiffness, and family history of migraines. Diagnosis not definitively established; discussion of migraine vs other primary headaches.

Management Plan:
- Analgesia: Ibuprofen used previously; patient was advised that up to two tablets can be taken up to three times daily. Dose/route not documented. Discussed stronger analgesics:
  - Naproxen (Rx option)
  - Paracetamol
  - Codeine
  - A prescription for a stronger analgesic option was offered today
- Adjuncts: Headache diary recommended to identify triggers.
- Eye considerations: Repeat eye exam recommended due to photophobia and ongoing visual symptoms.
- Activity/work: Patient advised to adjust screen brightness as needed and monitor for symptom changes.
- Follow-up: Return in 1–2 weeks; call/return sooner if symptoms worsen, new neurological symptoms, or vision changes.
- Prophylaxis: If headaches become more frequent, discussion of preventive therapy at the next visit.

Next Steps:
- If symptoms persist or worsen, schedule follow-up sooner.
- Consider prophylactic therapy at follow-up if attack frequency increases.
- Continue non-pharmacologic measures (hydration, screen adjustments) and monitor for triggers.

Patient Summary:
- A 26-year-old woman with a 3-day history of a progressive, mainly right-eye–predominant headache with photophobia and neck stiffness, not relieved by ibuprofen. Family history of migraines (mother and sister). A stronger analgesic option was offered today, with instructions to keep a headache diary and follow up in 1–2 weeks; eye exam and potential preventive therapy discussed as needed.

Key Takeaways:
- This pattern is compatible with migraine; stronger analgesic options were discussed, and a prescription may be issued today.
- Keep a headache diary to identify triggers; seek care sooner if vision changes or other neurological symptoms develop.
- Consider repeat eye exam given photophobia and eye strain concerns.

Next Steps:
- Initiate prescribed stronger analgesic if chosen; monitor response.
- Follow-up visit in 1–2 weeks; adjust plan based on frequency and severity.
- If headaches become more frequent, discuss preventive (prophylactic) therapy at follow-up.

- Missing elements: No vitals or full physical exam; no imaging or labs ordered; no explicit medication dosing details beyond general ibuprofen guidance; no medication reconciliation beyond patient-reported ibuprofen use.
- Internal conflicts: None identified in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Some conversational interruptions and incomplete phrasing; overall enough detail to derive the above, but some data (exact dose/formulation of ibuprofen, any recent imaging) is not provided.
